newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Envoys take Zaire peace initiative to Angola.
newsitem.headline: Envoys take Zaire peace initiative to Angola.

text.p: U.S. envoy Bill Richardson arrived in Luanda on Thursday to discuss the Zaire crisis with Angolan leaders, and perhaps South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki who was due in Angola to meet Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila.
Kabila entered the country earlier in the day, according to diplomatic sources.

Mbeki was on his way to Luanda to meet Kabila, whom he will accompany to face-to-face talks with Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko on board a South African navy ship in international waters off West Africa.

U.N. officials in New York said Richardson, Mbeki, Kabila as well as U.N. special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun might board the ship from Luanda. Separately, South African President Nelson Mandela was expected to leave home early on Friday for Point Noire on the coast of Congo, from where he would escort Mobutu to the ship.

Richardson, U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations, arrived mid-afternoon. "I've come here to meet with Angolan leaders. We have come to discuss the Zairean crisis," he said in a brief statement, but did not elaborate.

Diplomatic sources in the region have reported concern that Angola, struggling to establish its own fragile peace process, could be sucked into the Zaire war with government forces backing the rebels and former UNITA rebels backing the Zairean government.
Mandela said through a spokesman on Thursday that the talks, which he would chair, would be held on Friday.

Soon afterwards, the rebel alliance's shadow foreign minister Bizima Karaha said Kabila could only attend on Sunday. A spokesman for Mbeki, Mandela's chief negotiator in the Zaire peace initiative, said Karaha could have missed the latest developments

Richardson left Luanda's airport for the headquarters of the 6,000-strong U.N. peacekeeping mission for talks with the world body's acting special representative in Angola, Khaled Yassir, and other officials.

He was scheduled to meet Angolan Foreign Minister Venancio De Moura later, and diplomatic sources said Richardson was tentatively set to meet President Jose Eduardo dos Santos on Friday morning. A time had not been fixed.
A press aide accompanying Richardson told Reuters he could also meet Mbeki. "It's possible, we're going to try to," the aide said.
